docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: An aerospace franchise facing a product-safety interruption
Source: compiled from: https://investors.boeing.com/investors/news/press-release-details/2019/Boeing-Reports-Record-2018-Results-and-Provides-2019-Guidance/default.aspx; https://www.zeebiz.com/agencies/boeing-prepares-for-max-737-jets-sitting-outside-factory-as-deliveries-halted-90208
Date: 2019-03-15

Boeing designs and manufactures commercial aircraft, defense and space systems, and provides related services. Its commercial franchise benefits from engineering scale, certification requirements, a global supplier network and airlines' installed fleets. Airbus is the principal competitor in large commercial aircraft.

The company's total backlog at December2018 is approximatelyUS$490 billion, including nearly5,900 commercial aircraft. Backlog provides visibility into potential deliveries but is not immediately available cash or an unconditional claim on future profit. Customer financing, cancellations, production schedules and certification affect conversion.

The737 program serves the important single-aisle market. The MAX is its newest major version. A common fleet can help airlines with operating familiarity, training and maintenance, but safety confidence and regulatory permission are prerequisites for revenue service.

Following the March10 Ethiopian Airlines crash and the earlier Lion Air crash, authorities worldwide have grounded the MAX. Reuters's March15 account reports Boeing has suspended MAX deliveries while continuing production. The accident causes remain under investigation at this date.

The Reuters report says the broader737 line is producing52 aircraft per month and that MAX constitutes most output. This should not be misrepresented as52 delivered MAX aircraft per month after grounding. Physical production and cash delivery are now different.

Aircraft manufacturing has substantial working-capital commitments. Suppliers, labor and assembly costs may continue while customer delivery payments stop. Inventory accumulation can therefore impair cash conversion even before any final legal or engineering cost is known.

Defense and services provide other earnings streams, but they do not make the commercial interruption immaterial. Consolidated valuation must separate those businesses and their obligations from the temporarily unmarketable product.

The durable-franchise argument is strong: few companies can produce commercial aircraft at this scale, and demand for replacement/capacity aircraft has supported a large order book. The competing concern is whether the duration, technical remedy, certification process and customer response can be forecast with adequate confidence.

At the cutoff, no definitive common global return-to-service schedule or comprehensive cost estimate is available. The investment is not simply a familiar industrial cycle; it also requires an assessment of unresolved safety, regulatory and legal outcomes.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Record historical cash flow precedes an unquantified delivery interruption
Source: https://investors.boeing.com/investors/news/press-release-details/2019/Boeing-Reports-Record-2018-Results-and-Provides-2019-Guidance/default.aspx
Date: 2019-01-30

US$ billions except EPS. These figures and forecasts were published before the March grounding and must not be treated as a refreshed estimate of its consequences.

| Full-year metric | 2017 | 2018 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 94.005 | 101.127 |
| GAAP operating income | 10.344 | 11.987 |
| GAAP operating margin | 11.0% | 11.9% |
| Net earnings | 8.458 | 10.460 |
| GAAP diluted EPS | 13.85 | 17.85 |
| Core diluted EPS, non-GAAP | 12.33 | 16.01 |
| Operating cash flow | 13.346 | 15.322 |

FY2018 property/equipment additions are approximatelyUS$1.722 billion. CFO less those additions is approximatelyUS$13.600 billion, calculated. This is a useful historical cash measure, not an estimate of cash after an extended interruption in deliveries.

The company repurchased26.1 million shares forUS$9.0 billion during2018. Cash and marketable securities totaledUS$8.6 billion at year-end, consisting ofUS$7.7 billion cash andUS$0.9 billion marketable securities. Total consolidated debt was approximatelyUS$13.8 billion. Net debt after these liquid assets is aboutUS$5.2 billion, calculated.

The release gives586.2 million weighted-average diluted shares for2018. That is an annual earnings denominator, not the exact March15 common share count, particularly after repurchases. Any market capitalization using it must be labeled indicative.

January2019 guidance anticipatesUS$109.5–111.5 billion revenue, GAAP EPSUS$21.90–22.10, core EPSUS$19.90–20.10 andUS$17.0–17.5 billion operating cash flow. The forecasts depend on production and delivery assumptions established before the present event.

Commercial backlog is approximatelyUS$412.3 billion within theUS$490 billion consolidated backlog. An order book cannot by itself pay suppliers while deliveries are suspended. The timing and contract terms of progress payments versus final delivery payments need explicit modeling.

Historical accounting profitability and a modest net-debt figure indicate capacity to absorb some stress. They do not establish a maximum liability or a safe duration. Program economics, inventory, supplier commitments, customer remedies and possible legal costs are separate obligations from balance-sheet financial debt.
docs.D04_price_and_valuation.md:
Title: A selloff against a forecast that predates the shock
Source: compiled from: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BA?period1=1520726400&period2=1552694400&interval=1d; https://investors.boeing.com/investors/news/press-release-details/2019/Boeing-Reports-Record-2018-Results-and-Provides-2019-Guidance/default.aspx
Date: 2019-03-15

Historical unadjusted March15 close isUS$378.99. The preceding approximatelyone-year window recordsUS$446.01 high andUS$292.47 low. The close is approximately15.0% below that observed high; this is not a claim that the exact same percentage was lost between two weekly closes.

Session volume is26.70 million shares, well above the calculated20-session average10.19 million. Elevated trading reflects the sudden change in uncertainty. Liquidity in a large issuer does not make the business loss distribution small.

At2018 GAAP EPSUS$17.85, the stock trades approximately21.2x historical earnings. At core EPSUS$16.01, the multiple is23.7x. These denominators reflect a record operating year before the interruption.

January's2019 GAAP EPS guidanceUS$21.90–22.10 implies approximately17.1–17.3x; its core rangeUS$19.90–20.10 implies18.9–19.0x. Quoting only the lower forward multiple silently assumes pre-event delivery and profitability forecasts remain valid.

Using586.2 million annual weighted-average diluted shares gives indicative equity valueUS$222.2 billion. Adding year-end net debtUS$5.2 billion yields approximatelyUS$227.4 billion enterprise value before other adjustments. An exact current share count and complete enterprise-liability bridge are not recovered.

Historical CFO less capexUS$13.6 billion is approximately6.1% of this indicative equity value. It cannot be treated as an assured continuing cash yield while aircraft are built but not delivered.

A scenario model needs the duration of grounding, production/inventory response, engineering/training costs, customer compensation, legal exposure and subsequent delivery recovery. A short interruption and a more complex remedy can have very different outcomes even if the long-term duopoly survives.

Asset and franchise quality can support residual value, and defense/services can be valued separately. But no reliable contemporaneous aggregate cost ceiling or final return-to-service timetable is available. Applying a normal multiple to unaffected earnings and calling the price decline a margin of safety would skip the main underwriting question.

The valuation attraction is the possibility of a temporary problem in a scarce franchise. The uncertainty is whether cash losses and confidence effects are temporary, bounded and acceptable at the price.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: Safety, certification and cash timing cannot be reduced to one estimate
Source: compiled from: https://www.zeebiz.com/agencies/boeing-prepares-for-max-737-jets-sitting-outside-factory-as-deliveries-halted-90208; https://investors.boeing.com/investors/news/press-release-details/2019/Boeing-Reports-Record-2018-Results-and-Provides-2019-Guidance/default.aspx
Date: 2019-03-15

Reuters reports MAX deliveries have stopped while production continues. The immediate mechanical consequence is increasing finished inventory and a delay in customer payments. The commercial backlog remains substantial, but the company must convert it into aircraft that customers and regulators can accept.

Two fatal accidents involving a relatively new model have created a safety investigation, not just a marketing problem. At this cutoff, the evidence does not establish a complete engineering explanation, the final remedy or approval dates across all relevant jurisdictions.

Keeping production running may preserve supplier continuity and avoid costly stop/start disruptions. It also consumes cash and physical storage space. Reducing production may protect liquidity but create its own industrial and contractual costs. Neither option is costless.

The January results release had emphasized expected record deliveries, higher2019 profits and cash flow. Those forecasts relied on planned commercial deliveries, with other businesses also contributing. They show why investors valued the franchise highly, but are not a forecast incorporating the current grounding.

The bull case is a technically fixable interruption, eventual deliveries from a deep backlog, and a duopoly with high entry barriers. If confidence returns quickly, delayed cash may be recovered rather than permanently lost. Existing defense and service operations provide additional value.

The bear case is broader than a quarter of deferred deliveries. Possible redesign, training, certification differences, legal claims and lost customer confidence may change costs and schedules. An activist board seat cannot itself supply a regulator's approval or an independent accident finding.

It would also be wrong to assume an unlimited liability simply because the facts are uncertain. The honest gap is that a reliable range has not yet been established. The investor needs stress cases rather than an unsupported binary prediction that either nothing is wrong or the franchise is destroyed.

Key monitoring items are the investigation evidence, regulator requirements, customer acceptance, production decisions and cash conversion. No subsequent production halt, final settlements or return-to-service date is included. The current decision must be made with an unusually wide range of possible near-term outcomes.
docs.D08_pershing_square_context.md:
Title: A durable moat does not automatically imply a predictable investment outcome
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2014/09/08113002/PSH-Annual-Report.pdf; https://www.zeebiz.com/agencies/boeing-prepares-for-max-737-jets-sitting-outside-factory-as-deliveries-halted-90208
Date: 2019-03-15

Pershing Square's2014 annual report, published inMarch2015, sets out a general preference for “simple, predictable, free-cash-flow generative businesses.” The purpose is to identify enterprises whose economics and investment outcomes can be assessed with high confidence, not merely companies with recognizable brands.

The same discussion focuses on businesses whose values are not materially driven by “extrinsic factors we cannot control.” It cites the economic cycle and other external influences. This does not assert that every regulatory exposure is disqualifying or that the manager has never owned a special situation.

Boeing has formidable industrial barriers and a commercially important installed base. Those qualities support one part of the framework. The different question is how much a current owner can know about cash generation and claims during a product-safety grounding.

An ordinary operating activist can work on incentives, costs, leadership and capital allocation. It cannot predetermine an accident investigation, certification standard or global approval schedule. Those constraints distinguish a company-specific cost problem from an event whose resolution depends on independent authorities and technical evidence.

Pershing's report also favors companies that can survive and thrive without continuous access to capital markets. Boeing's historical liquidity provides resilience, but required funding during a long delivery pause must be modeled separately from record2018 operating cash flow.

A responsible valuation can recognize the long-term duopoly without asserting the current cost is known. A scenario with several months of delayed deliveries is not equivalent to a scenario with new engineering/training obligations and materially changed customer behavior.

No authenticated pre-March15 Ackman company-specific view or exact contemporary Pershing liquidity reconciliation is supplied in these sources. A reader should not infer a manager's actual decision from the fact that the company resembles another large industrial holding.

The framework invites a distinction between an attractive scarce asset and a sufficiently bounded risk at today's price. Waiting for a narrower set of facts is analytically different from forecasting permanent failure, and a business can remain valuable while being unsuitable for a concentrated position at a particular moment.

drivers.driver: Unresolved safety, certification and liability range defeats high-confidence cash-flow underwriting even in a duopoly.
Independent regulator/technical outcomes cannot be delivered through ordinary operating activism. The post-shock risk must be bounded rather than assumed temporary from historical earnings.
Pre-grounding cash guidance is not funding capacity under a prolonged delivery pause; financing resilience needs separate stress analysis.
drivers.quote: do not need access to the capital markets to survive and thrive

valuation.downside_case: Prolonged grounding, significant market share loss, and liability costs exhausting the $8.6B liquidity buffer.

drivers.driver: The Company operates in a dominant, high-barrier-to-entry commercial aircraft duopoly with a substantial 5,900 aircraft backlog [D01, D05].
We have acquired our stake at a 17.3x pre-shock forward GAAP EPS multiple, representing a 15% drawdown due to temporary regulatory fears [D03].
The 737 MAX grounding is a temporary operational disruption that does not impair the long-term intrinsic value of the franchise [D01, D03].
Normalized EPS growth will be driven by the clearing of the 5,900 aircraft backlog and the resumption of deliveries once the engineering fix is certified [D01, D05].

kill_criteria: Permanent revocation of 737 MAX airworthiness certification by global regulators.
Material loss of long-term commercial aircraft market share to Airbus (e.g., persistent <40% backlog share).
Legal liabilities or customer compensation requirements exceeding $20 billion, threatening the balance sheet solvency.
Management failure to maintain the industrial moat, specifically losing dominance in large commercial aircraft production.
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the 737 MAX engineering issues are systemic and unfixable, or that liability costs will fundamentally destroy the company’s capital-light competitive advantages.
final.memo:
The Company is a dominant, free-cash-flow-generative industrial leader that controls one-half of the global commercial aircraft duopoly [D01, D05]. With a backlog of 5,900 aircraft and essential engineering scale, the business possesses the long-term durability and predictability that meet our investment standards [D01, D05].

The market has currently panicked due to the 737 MAX grounding, viewing a temporary engineering and regulatory hurdle as an existential threat to the company’s competitive moat [D01, D03, D04]. We believe the market is wrong; this is a fixable, albeit serious, regulatory setback for a mission-critical franchise, not a permanent impairment of intrinsic value [D01, D03].

We have initiated this position at a 17.3x pre-shock forward GAAP EPS multiple, a valuation that significantly under-reflects the normalized earning power of the company [D03]. Assuming a return to historical delivery levels, we project normalized EPS of $28.00–$32.00 in the coming years, suggesting an IRR of approximately 22% based on a 20x exit multiple [D02, D03].

The catalyst for value realization is the eventual regulatory re-certification of the 737 MAX and the subsequent clearing of the inventory that has constrained cash flows [D01, D02, D05]. Our role is to remain patient as these operational flows normalize, knowing that the company’s $8.6 billion liquidity position provides a sufficient buffer to manage the current liabilities [D02, D03].

Risks include a prolonged grounding or liability costs that could threaten the balance sheet, though these remain unlikely given the company’s entrenched duopoly position [D01, D02, D03]. Should legal or regulatory risks materialize beyond our $20 billion stress-test ceiling, we would reconsider the position [D02, D03].

We are sizing this at 8% of NAV, reflecting our high conviction in the recovery of this compounder despite the current market dislocation [D03, D05]. We view this as a rare opportunity to own a world-class, dominant franchise at a mid-teens multiple of its future earnings potential [D03].
uncited_claims: The Company is a rare opportunity to own a world-class, dominant franchise at a mid-teens multiple of its future earnings potential.

valuation.entry_multiple: 18.9x NTM EPS based on January 2019 guidance
valuation.eps_path: Core EPS recovers to guided levels with 10% normalized growth post-recovery
valuation.downside_case: Prolonged grounding erodes balance sheet through liabilities but fails to impair long-term duopoly value

drivers.driver: Boeing is a dominant global duopolist with high barriers to entry, benefiting from long-term secular growth in aviation [D01].
The market has mispriced the 737 MAX grounding as a permanent impairment rather than a fixable, transitory regulatory hurdle [D01], [D04].
We are able to acquire a stake at approximately 18.9x NTM EPS following a 15% drawdown from recent highs [D02], [D03].
The company maintains a strong balance sheet with only US$5.2 billion in net debt, providing a cushion for near-term operational costs [D02].

kill_criteria: Technical or software fix fails to gain regulatory certification within 12 months
Evidence of systemic manufacturing or design culture failure beyond the 737 MAX
Liability costs exceed the company's ability to fund operations without significant equity dilution or debt restructuring
Permanent shift in airline demand away from Boeing products toward Airbus
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the engineering and regulatory issues are systemic and unfixable, leading to a permanent loss of market share to Airbus or a fundamental destruction of the company's long-term earnings power.
final.memo:
The Boeing Company operates as one of two global manufacturers of large commercial aircraft, a position defined by immense engineering barriers, regulatory certification requirements, and an entrenched installed base [D01]. This duopoly structure creates a business with highly predictable, secular demand that we view as a quintessential quality compounder [D01].

Currently, the market is reacting to the tragic 737 MAX accidents and the subsequent global grounding of the fleet [D01], [D04]. We believe the market is misinterpreting this as a permanent impairment to the franchise, rather than a fixable technical and regulatory challenge [D01], [D04]. This dislocation has provided an opportunity to acquire shares at a 15% discount to recent highs [D03].

Our valuation at an entry multiple of approximately 18.9x NTM EPS reflects the potential for the business to return to its pre-crisis guidance of US$19.90-20.10 per share [D02], [D03]. With a normalized growth algorithm of 10% and a terminal multiple of 22x, we believe the investment offers a compelling IRR [D01], [D02].

The primary catalyst for value realization is the successful certification of the technical fix and the resumption of deliveries, allowing for the normalization of free cash flow [D01], [D02]. We view our role as quiet, long-term investors awaiting the company's return to its historical operational strength [D01].

The primary risk remains a prolonged grounding that could test the company's balance sheet through legal and compensation liabilities [D01], [D02]. However, with only US$5.2 billion in net debt, the company is well-positioned to manage these transitory costs [D02].

We are initiating a position today with an initial 3% target, scaling toward an 8% core holding as we gain confidence in the re-entry of the MAX fleet [D03]. This size is appropriate for a liquid, mega-cap industrial and aligns with our strategy of capturing value during temporary dislocations in dominant franchises [D01], [D03].
